escena: SCENE (Efeonce office, Santiago, high floor, late morning): the Efeonce office kitchen, from a stool at its oak island, seen from the chair of someone sitting there on a video call — camera at SEATED EYE LEVEL (about 1.15 m), 28 mm lens at f/5.6, like a good webcam view, looking straight at the warm-white matte plaster kitchen wall 2.5 m away, with a long oak counter along its base; horizon level, verticals straight. RIGHT THIRD: Image 2 is the final artwork of the lettering on that wall above the counter — a small line and a large line with its magenta sphere as the period — reproduce it exactly as cut matte navy vinyl letters applied flat on the plaster. Under it on the counter: a sleek current-generation stainless espresso machine, two plain white ceramic mugs and the official Efeonce logo from Image 1 as a small solid DEEP NAVY (#023C70, dark ink blue, never royal blue) desk object about 24 cm wide and 6 cm tall, standing upright on the counter at the right, between the mugs and the espresso machine, turned towards the camera: product placement, reproduced exactly (every letter of «efeonce», the ship emblem with its orbit ring, its cuts and its three small windows), satin finish, crisp bevel. LEFT THIRD: Image 3 is the final artwork of a framed «employee of the month» print; hang it on the wall at head height as a real black-framed print under glass with a faint reflection, reproduced exactly: the header, the portrait of the woman in her navy Efeonce uniform jacket with the embroidered emblem and the Efeonce lanyard, and her name with its sphere. LIGHT: hard sun from the RIGHT through a window out of frame crosses the kitchen as a visible shaft; a thin wisp of steam rising from the espresso machine catches it. The centre of the wall stays calm and bare. TRACES OF WORK: a spoon left on a saucer, a mug upside down on a drying rack. Nothing else on the walls: no posters, no clocks, no extra signage and no extra text anywhere. TEXT EXCEPTION: the logo from Image 1 and the artworks from Image 2 and Image 3 are the ONLY readable marks in the picture; they stay crisp and fully legible, every letter and word exactly as in the references, never blurred, altered or translated; every other screen, paper or label stays illegible by physical means.
